Hidden Man of the Heart
thuh HID-uhn man uhv thuh hart
noun
From 1 Peter 3:4; the inward, spiritual self, the true adorning of the believer, especially the godly woman.

Biblical Definition

The hidden man of the heart is Peter’s phrase for the inward, spiritual self—the true and abiding character of the soul as opposed to the outward, visible adorning of the body. Charging Christian wives, the apostle writes that their adorning should not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel; but let it be the hidden man of the heart, in that which is not corruptible, even the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price. The hidden man of the heart is the renewed inner self, the new creature, whose true beauty is invisible to the eye but precious to God. Its ornament is not gold or fine clothing, which perish, but the incorruptible graces of the Spirit—a meek and quiet spirit, of great price in His sight. The principle is not that outward neatness is forbidden, but that the heart, not the body, is the seat of true and lasting beauty, and that the believer—and especially the godly woman—is to give chief care to the adorning of the inner self. The dictionary honors the hidden man of the heart as the Scripture’s account of true beauty—the renewed inner self, adorned with the incorruptible ornament of a meek and quiet spirit—against an age obsessed with the corruptible adorning of the outward body, and presses the godly to seek that beauty which is in the sight of God of great price.

Key Scripture

1Pe 3:4 — "But let it be the hidden man of the heart, in that which is not corruptible, even the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price."

1Pe 3:3 — "Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel;"

1Sa 16:7 — "But the LORD said unto Samuel, Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature; because I have refused him: for the LORD seeth not as man seeth; for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart."

2Co 4:16 — "For which cause we faint not; but though our outward man perish, yet the inward man is renewed day by day."

Modern Corruption

True worth is sought in outward appearance and adornment; Scripture sets the hidden man of the heart, adorned with a meek and quiet spirit, as the beauty of great price.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition beyond the cult of the outward. The corruption is the obsession, ancient and modern, with the outward adorning—seeking worth, identity, and beauty in the appearance of the body, the hair, the apparel, the corruptible things that perish. An age that lavishes endless care on the outward man and neglects the inner has inverted the values of Scripture, which prizes what God prizes: not the visible, but the hidden man of the heart.

The principle to recover is that true and lasting beauty is inward and spiritual. Peter directs the godly woman’s adorning not to the outward plaiting of hair and wearing of gold (1 Pet 3:3), but to the hidden man of the heart, in that which is not corruptible, the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price (1 Pet 3:4). For the LORD seeth not as man seeth; man looks on the outward appearance, but the LORD looks on the heart (1 Sam 16:7). The outward man perishes, but the inward man is renewed day by day (2 Cor 4:16). This is no forbidding of neatness, but a reordering of the heart’s care: to seek above all the incorruptible beauty of the renewed inner self, precious in the sight of God.
